a.summary: Five of the six new `signInOrder` instance methods bypass `signInOrder(SequencedCollection)` and delegate straight to the deprecated members, so overriding the surviving name yields an internally inconsistent object today and a silent behaviour flip when the deprecated names are removed.

b.summary: The five secondary `signInOrder*` entry points bypass an override of `signInOrder(SequencedCollection)`, while the five secondary `signByKey*` entry points honor an override of `signByKey(Collection)` — opposite, undocumented delegation policies introduced in the same commit.
b.failure_scenario: A consumer subclass adds policy to the new, non-deprecated name: `class AuditedTx extends ... { @Override public void signInOrder(SequencedCollection<Signer> s) { audit(s); super.signInOrder(s); } }`. `tx.signInOrder(signers)` runs `audit`. `tx.signInOrder(blockHash, signers)` does NOT: line 856 calls `sign(recentBlockHash, signers)` -> `sign(SequencedCollection)`, skipping the override entirely; the transaction is still signed, so the omission is silent. The mirror-image subclass overriding `signByKey(Collection)` sees its override run for all six entry points, because 896/902 call `signByKey(signers)`. I confirmed both outcomes by compiling and running a faithful model: `signInOrder(hash, signers) -> [sign(SequencedCollection)]` versus `signByKey(hash, signers) -> [OVERRIDE signByKey, sign(Collection)]`.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
